cases.title: Drag initiation captures product title and price
cases.description: When a user starts dragging a product <li> element (e.g., data-testid="product-item-1") the dragstart event fires and the dataTransfer payload contains the correct product title and price extracted from the associated data-testid elements.

cases.title: Drop into cart updates title, price, and quantity UI
cases.description: Dropping a draggable product into the designated drop area (id="div1", data-testid="drop-area") adds the item to the cart and populates the title in .box2, unit price in .box3, and sets quantity to 1 in .box1.

cases.title: Multiple distinct products update cart and total
cases.description: After sequentially dropping two different products into the drop area, each product appears with correct title, price, and quantity (1). The total displayed in #allMoney equals the sum of both prices, formatted with a leading '$' and two decimal places.

cases.title: Repeated product drops increment quantity and total
cases.description: Dropping the same product three times results in a single cart entry where the quantity in .box1 is 3, the title and unit price remain unchanged, and the total in #allMoney reflects price × 3, correctly formatted.

cases.title: Total price formatting after mixed drops
cases.description: After adding a mixture of distinct and repeated products, the system calculates the aggregate total, formats it to exactly two decimal places with a leading '$', and displays the result in the <div id="allMoney"> element.

cases.title: Non-draggable element does not trigger drag logic
cases.description: Attempting to drag an element that lacks draggable="true" (e.g., a plain <div>) does not fire a dragstart event and no dataTransfer payload is created.

cases.title: Dropping outside designated area leaves cart unchanged
cases.description: When a product is dragged and dropped on an element other than the drop area (#div1), the cart UI (title, price, quantity) and total remain unchanged and no errors are thrown.

opinions.feedback: The test suite covers the core drag‑and‑drop flow and total‑price calculations well, and the cases are largely distinct. However, three cases rely on behavior that the specifications do not guarantee, turning them into blockers. Adjust the requirements to explicitly define non‑draggable handling, aggregation of repeated items, and out‑of‑area drop behavior, or revise the test cases to align with the existing specs. Once clarified, the suite will be fully executable and risk‑free.
confirmed_blockers: G-006 – The requirement R‑1 only defines drag behavior for product <li> elements; it does not specify that non‑draggable elements must not fire a dragstart event, so the expected “no dragstart” behavior is unsupported.

G-004 – Requirement R‑3 states the system supports adding repeated products but does not define that they must be aggregated into a single entry with a quantity field. Expecting .box1 to show a quantity of 3 is therefore outside the specified behavior.

G-007 – The requirements describe the correct handling of drops into the designated drop area (R‑3) but give no guidance on what should happen when a drop occurs elsewhere. Expecting the cart to remain unchanged and no errors to be thrown is not covered, making the test case’s expected outcome unsupported.

analysis.analysis: The requirements define three functional areas: (1) drag initiation on <li> product items (draggable="true") must fire a dragstart event and capture the product title and price; (2) dropping a product into the designated drop area (id="div1", data-testid="drop-area") must update the cart UI showing title in .box2, unit price in .box3 and quantity in .box1, supporting both new and repeated items; (3) total price must be summed (price × quantity), formatted to two decimal places with a leading '$' and displayed in #allMoney. Testable behaviours include verifying the dataTransfer payload, UI updates after single and multiple drops, quantity increment for repeated drops, and correct total calculation/formatting. Boundaries and edge cases: missing data‑testids, non‑draggable elements, drops outside the target, invalid price formats, large quantities, and currency formatting. Normal paths cover correct drag‑drop sequences leading to proper UI and total updates. Abnormal paths cover missing attributes, non‑draggable drags, out‑of‑zone drops, and malformed prices, which should not break the system. Ambiguities: format of the drag data payload, whether repeated drops aggregate into a single cart row or multiple rows, exact DOM hierarchy for .box* elements, handling of non‑numeric prices, and fixed currency symbol expectations. The critic feedback flags three blockers: unclear UI aggregation for repeated drops (G‑004), unspecified behavior for non‑draggable elements (G‑006), and undefined handling of drops outside the drop area (G‑007). These need to be added to the requirements before the associated test cases can be validated.
